        if (stack is null || stack.GetChildren().OfType<ResearchOverlay>()
            .Any(screen => !screen.IsQueuedForDeletion()))
        {
            return;
        }

        stack.Push(new ResearchOverlay
        {
            Name = "FieldNotesResearchOverlay"
        });
    }

    public override void _Ready()
    {
        SetAnchorsAndOffsetsPreset(LayoutPreset.FullRect);
        MouseFilter = MouseFilterEnum.Stop;

        var center = new CenterContainer();
        center.SetAnchorsAndOffsetsPreset(LayoutPreset.FullRect);
        AddChild(center);

        var panel = new PanelContainer
        {
            CustomMinimumSize = new Vector2(860f, 520f)
        };
        center.AddChild(panel);

        var margin = new MarginContainer();
        margin.AddThemeConstantOverride("margin_left", 32);
        margin.AddThemeConstantOverride("margin_top", 28);
        margin.AddThemeConstantOverride("margin_right", 32);
        margin.AddThemeConstantOverride("margin_bottom", 28);
        panel.AddChild(margin);

        var column = new VBoxContainer();
        column.AddThemeConstantOverride("separation", 20);
        margin.AddChild(column);

        column.AddChild(new Label
        {
            Text = "Field Research",
            HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center
        });

        column.AddChild(new RichTextLabel
        {
            BbcodeEnabled = true,
            FitContent = true,
            CustomMinimumSize = new Vector2(760f, 350f),
            Text = BuildSummary()
        });

        _closeButton = new Button
        {
            Text = "Close"
        };
        _closeButton.Pressed += Close;
        column.AddChild(_closeButton);
    }

    public void AfterOverlayOpened()
    {
    }

    public void AfterOverlayClosed()
    {
        QueueFree();
    }

    public void AfterOverlayShown()
    {
        Visible = true;
        _closeButton?.GrabFocus();
    }

    public void AfterOverlayHidden()
    {
        Visible = false;
    }

    private static string BuildSummary()
    {
        return $"[b]Loaded model database[/b]\n\n" +
               $"Cards: {ModelDb.AllCards.Count()}\n" +
               $"Potions: {ModelDb.AllPotions.Count()}\n" +
               $"Relics: {ModelDb.AllRelics.Count()}\n" +
               $"Events: {ModelDb.AllEvents.Count()}\n\n" +
               "This panel is hosted by NOverlayStack and uses its shared backstop.";
    }

    private void Close()
    {
        var stack = NOverlayStack.Instance;
        if (stack is null)
        {
            QueueFree();
            return;
        }

        stack.Remove(this);
    }
}

docs.title: Lifecycle Meaning
docs.text:
NOverlayStack.Push performs more than AddChild:

  • hides the previous overlay
  • adds the new control to the overlay branch
  • places the shared backstop relative to the overlay
  • updates ActiveScreenContext
  • calls open and shown callbacks

Remove calls hidden and closed callbacks, reveals the previous overlay, and updates focus context. It does not guarantee that an arbitrary custom control frees itself, so the example calls QueueFree in AfterOverlayClosed.

Visible is changed in shown and hidden callbacks because stacked overlays remain in the tree while another overlay is above them.

docs.title: Focus And Input
docs.text:
DefaultFocusedControl lets the active screen context identify the close button. The shown callback also calls GrabFocus so keyboard and controller navigation begin in a usable state.

For a larger panel:

  • define explicit focus neighbors for grids
  • provide a cancel action that calls Close
  • preserve the previously focused native control if returning focus is important
  • do not process gameplay hotkeys while a text field or modal is active

The NetScreenType.None value means the example does not advertise itself as one of the game's synchronized network screens. A multiplayer UI that changes shared game state needs a separate network and command design; changing the enum does not create synchronization.

docs.title: Native Widgets Versus Plain Godot Controls
docs.text:
Plain Button, Label, and containers are sufficient to demonstrate hierarchy, but they do not automatically match STS2 typography, sounds, hover motion, or controller behavior.

For native presentation:

  1. inspect a nearby native screen in sts2.dll
  2. inspect its .tscn and theme resources in the PCK
  3. instantiate native button or label scenes rather than copying private fields
  4. preserve the overlay lifecycle shown here

Do not start by cloning an entire complex native screen. First make a small overlay open, focus, hide, close, and free correctly.

docs.title: Reusing Card And Relic Screens
docs.text:
NCardLibrary and NRelicCollection are NSubmenu screens, not IOverlayScreen implementations. They need submenu-stack ownership and the visual geometry used by their native caller.

If a custom overlay launches one of them:

  • keep the overlay as the visual and input context that launched the flow
  • create the native screen through its factory
  • assign the correct submenu stack
  • attach it to the visual host used by the native compendium path
  • let the submenu stack push and pop it
  • keep tooltip layers above custom dimming controls

The current NRunSubmenuStack already hosts these screens as children. Prefer its GetSubmenuType<T>() or PushSubmenuType<T>() factories instead of duplicating their creation and attachment logic. NSubmenuStack.Push alone does not add a newly created screen to the scene tree.

docs.title: Overlay never opens
docs.text: Check that NRun._Ready was patched, the controller exists under the current run, and NOverlayStack.Instance is non-null.

docs.title: Overlay opens twice
docs.text: Check both controller duplication and existing overlay children. Checking only Peek() misses a custom overlay underneath another screen. The example ignores queued-for-deletion children so a closing overlay does not block the next open indefinitely.

docs.title: Tooltips are hidden
docs.text: The custom backdrop or panel is above the native tooltip layer. Compare sibling order with a vanilla overlay and move only the custom host, not the tooltip system.

docs.title: Geometry is shifted or clipped
docs.text: The control is under a content-sized parent rather than the viewport-sized overlay branch. Log parent size, global position, and anchors.

docs.title: Close leaves an invisible blocker
docs.text: The overlay was removed visually but not from the stack, or it was removed from the stack but not freed. Use NOverlayStack.Remove and free in AfterOverlayClosed.

docs.title: Validation Matrix
docs.text:
Verify:

  1. one controller is attached for each run scene
  2. F8 opens only one overlay
  3. the shared backstop blocks room input
  4. the close button receives keyboard and controller focus
  5. another native overlay can cover and reveal the custom overlay
  6. close removes the screen from the stack and frees the node
  7. map, rewards, hover tips, and pause screens still layer correctly
  8. starting a new run creates a fresh controller without stale static state

Once this lifecycle is stable, replace the generated controls with a packed scene or expand the panel into a model browser, settings page, picker, or debugging surface.

docs.title: Related Sections
docs.text: Review overlay ownership and tooltip ordering when extending this panel. Use the iteration loop to test each scene-lifecycle change.

docs.title: 15. State, Saves, Cloning, And Randomness
docs.text:
A model becomes considerably more demanding once it remembers something. A relic that counts played cards must distinguish its canonical definition from its owned instance, preserve progress across saves, update its counter, and avoid counting another player's actions. Random effects introduce another requirement: the same run state must lead to the same decisions after a reload.

This chapter follows those boundaries in v0.107.1. The examples extend the custom relic tutorial and the act event tutorial.

docs.title: Choose The Lifetime First
docs.text:
Before choosing a field, decide what its value belongs to:

State Appropriate lifetime Base amount or threshold Canonical definition and dynamic variables Relic progress across rooms Mutable relic instance with saved properties A temporary target during resolution Mutable instance, cleared at the relevant lifecycle boundary Panel selection or animation progress UI node, recreated with the panel A sequence of random decisions Seeded gameplay RNG with an explicitly owned lifetime

A static field belongs to the process. It is shared across copies and players, survives scene replacement, and is not automatically restored from a run save. It is therefore a poor default for gameplay progress.

docs.title: A Relic That Remembers Played Cards
docs.text:
The following relic draws one card after every fifth owner play reported to AfterCardPlayedLate while combat is still in progress. Its progress carries between combats and is persisted in the run save. A play that ends combat may not reach this hook and therefore may not advance the counter.

using System.Threading.Tasks;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Commands;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Relics;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.GameActions.Multiplayer;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Models;
using MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Saves.Runs;

namespace FieldNotes.Relics;

public sealed class ResearchLedgerRelic : RelicModel
{
    private const int Threshold = 5;
    private int _cardsRecorded;

    public override RelicRarity Rarity => RelicRarity.Uncommon;
    public override bool ShowCounter => true;
    public override int DisplayAmount => CardsRecorded;

    public override string PackedIconPath =>
        "res://FieldNotes/images/relics/research_ledger.png";

    protected override string PackedIconOutlinePath =>
        "res://FieldNotes/images/relics/research_ledger_outline.png";

    protected override string BigIconPath =>
        "res://FieldNotes/images/relics/research_ledger_large.png";

    [SavedProperty]
    public int CardsRecorded
    {
        get => _cardsRecorded;
        set
        {
            AssertMutable();
            _cardsRecorded = ((value % Threshold) + Threshold) % Threshold;
            InvokeDisplayAmountChanged();
        }
    }

    public override async Task AfterCardPlayedLate(
        PlayerChoiceContext choiceContext,
        CardPlay cardPlay)
    {
        if (cardPlay.Card.Owner != Owner)
        {
            return;
        }

        CardsRecorded++;
        if (CardsRecorded != 0)
        {
            return;
        }

        Flash();
        await CardPileCmd.Draw(choiceContext, 1m, Owner);
    }
}

Register ResearchLedgerRelic in SharedRelicPool during the initializer, using the same registration pattern as the earlier relic. Supply all three images and add these entries to the mod's relics.json:

{
  "RESEARCH_LEDGER_RELIC.title": "Research Ledger",
  "RESEARCH_LEDGER_RELIC.description": "After every 5 card plays you complete while combat remains in progress, draw 1 card. Progress carries between combats.",
  "RESEARCH_LEDGER_RELIC.flavor": "The fifth observation always raises another question."
}

The owner check matters because hook dispatch can present actions performed by other players. The example counts every play that reaches this hook for the owner, including applicable automatic plays and replays; it does not claim to count only cards played from the hand. If that distinction matters to the design, inspect the current CardPlay construction and the relevant vanilla effect before adding a filter.

The counter resets before drawing. Reactions triggered by the draw therefore observe the next cycle's state. Keeping the draw in the awaited command chain preserves the game's choice context and sequencing. At this point the played card has not necessarily left the Play pile; the late hook is not a notification that final pile movement has completed.

This example intentionally delays its draw until after ordinary post-play listeners. Use ordinary AfterCardPlayed if that ordering is not part of the desired effect.

docs.title: What SavedProperty Actually Saves
docs.text:
SerializableRelic stores a model ID plus an optional SavedProperties payload. That payload reads attributed properties through reflection and records their property names. The backing field is not the serialization contract; CardsRecorded is.

The current writer explicitly handles these value families:

  • int, bool, and string
  • enums, encoded as integers
  • int[] and enum arrays
  • ModelId
  • SerializableCard
  • List<SerializableCard>

Do not infer arbitrary-object support from the JSON-based save format. A dictionary, List<int>, Godot node, or custom class is not automatically supported by this attribute. Unsupported non-null values cause a serialization exception. Null values are warned about rather than stored as ordinary supported values.

Use simple saved values and reconstruct derived state from them. Keep scene nodes, textures, event delegates, and animation tasks out of the save representation. The fact that a property saves also does not make arbitrary mutations into multiplayer commands: state still needs to change through deterministic gameplay flow.

docs.title: Save Compatibility Is An Interface
docs.text:
Two names become persistent interfaces:

  1. the model entry derived from the class name
  2. each attributed property name

Renaming ResearchLedgerRelic or CardsRecorded can invalidate or lose old state unless explicit migration handles it. A renamed property is not automatically mapped to its replacement.

Changing a threshold is also a gameplay migration. The example normalizes a loaded value into the new counter range, but that policy changes the player's progress. Choose and test a deliberate policy rather than treating a successful deserialize as proof of compatibility.

Test a run saved with progress 4, reload it in a fresh process, then play one card. Test the same sequence across a combat boundary. The draw should occur exactly once, and the displayed count should match the restored state.

docs.title: Cloning Is A Separate Operation
docs.text:
Serialization and cloning solve different problems. AbstractModel.MutableClone begins with MemberwiseClone, sets mutability, calls DeepCloneFields, then calls AfterCloned. A shallow copy duplicates a reference to a collection or delegate; it does not duplicate the referenced object.

For a custom mutable collection, the pattern is:

protected override void DeepCloneFields()
{
    base.DeepCloneFields();
    _visitedEntries = new HashSet<string>(_visitedEntries);
}

This is a fragment for a model that declares _visitedEntries as HashSet<string>. It protects clones from sharing the same set. It does not make the set a supported saved property.

For events declared by the custom model, clear the copied delegates:

protected override void AfterCloned()
{
    base.AfterCloned();
    ProgressChanged = null;
}

Here ProgressChanged is an event declared by that model. Clearing its copied delegate prevents a clone from notifying subscribers attached to the source instance and retaining UI objects through those subscribers.

Prefer the model-specific ToMutable() factory when obtaining a gameplay instance from a canonical definition. ClonePreservingMutability() returns the canonical instance unchanged, or clones an already mutable instance. These semantics matter in preview and inspect code: do not assume every operation called "clone" produces an independent mutable model.

docs.title: Randomness Has State Too
docs.text:
The game's Rng exposes a seed and a counter. Reproducing a sequence requires both the same initial state and the same calls in the same order. A tooltip that rolls an outcome on hover can therefore change gameplay even when nothing visible has been selected.

Rng.Chaotic is explicitly non-deterministic across saves. Reserve it for effects that do not influence gameplay. Avoid System.Random, clock-based seeds, or Godot random functions for rewards, damage, event options, or target selection that must be reproducible.

docs.title: Event Rolls
docs.text:
EventModel provides a per-event Rng after the event begins and receives its owner. It is unavailable on the canonical event. Roll dynamic event values in CalculateVars, then use the resulting value for both text and the selected effect.

For the existing observatory event, replace its fixed gold calculation with this override:

public override void CalculateVars()
{
    DynamicVars.Gold.BaseValue = Rng.NextInt(40, 81);
}

The upper bound is exclusive: this produces 40 through 80. Do not roll again in the option's getter or click handler; otherwise the displayed offer and the actual reward can disagree.

docs.title: Content-Specific Streams
docs.text:
The current API also offers:

Rng(Player player, ModelId id, uint mixin = 0, int counter = 0)

Its seed derives from the run seed, player slot, model entry, and optional mixin. Player slot is used rather than network ID so a changed network identity need not change a daily-run outcome.

Creating this RNG again with identical arguments starts the same sequence. That can be useful for a stable offer, but it does not provide a fresh roll for each occurrence. For repeated occurrences, own the stream explicitly or use a deterministic occurrence mixin and preserve the state needed to reconstruct it. Do not call runtime GetHashCode() to manufacture a stable mixin.

Candidate order is part of the random algorithm. When selecting from a set of models, construct the candidate list in a deterministic order, such as ordinal model-entry order, before drawing an index. The same seed cannot compensate for different lists or different list ordering on peers.

docs.title: Useful Failure Signatures
docs.text: Symptom Likely boundary to inspect Progress disappears after restart Missing saved property or changed property name Two instances share progress Static field or shallow-copied mutable reference Preview triggers the original UI Copied event delegate Save fails only after obtaining an item Unsupported saved-property value type Offer changes when hovered RNG consumed in a presentation path Same item always rolls the same result RNG recreated with identical seed arguments Multiplayer counts other players' cards Missing ownership filter in the hook

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The full relic example is intended for the same assembly and resources as the earlier content examples. Check compilation separately from runtime behavior:

  1. grant two mutable instances in an isolated test and confirm their counters are independent
  2. play four cards, save, restart, and confirm the fifth triggers one draw
  3. cross a combat boundary with partial progress
  4. inspect and hover the relic repeatedly; neither operation should change progress or gameplay RNG
  5. test another player's card plays in multiplayer
  6. test a save from the previous mod release after changing a saved field or threshold

Use save troubleshooting for file locations and hook selection for resolution timing. Compilation verifies API use; these scenarios verify the intended behavior.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Hook.AfterCardPlayed currently invokes model listeners in two passes:

  1. AfterCardPlayed(PlayerChoiceContext, CardPlay)

The late pass follows ordinary post-play listeners for each individual play. Both passes precede final result-pile movement and are skipped if combat has ended. See card resolution.

docs.title: Version And Loader Types
docs.text:
ModDependency contains JSON fields id and optional min_version; ModManifest.dependencies is List<ModDependency>?. ModManifest.ReadFromStream(Stream, out List<LocString>?) reads manifests and migrates legacy string dependencies with a diagnostic.

ModManagerState values are None, Initialized, and Skipped. This is loader initialization state, separate from each Mod.state. Skipped covers test/AOT paths and the nomods command-line option. Per-mod state, errors, and parsed version should be inspected when diagnosing compatibility.

See versioned manifests for the authoring contract.

docs.title: Appendix B. Release Package Patterns
docs.text: Older community archives show several layouts, but the current loader contract is determined by v0.107.1, not by historical package contents.

docs.title: Current Install-Ready Pattern
docs.text:
mods/
  MyMod/
    MyMod.json
    MyMod.dll
    MyMod.pck

The external JSON is required for discovery. The DLL and PCK are required only when has_dll or has_pck is true.

docs.title: Other Archive Shapes
docs.text:
Historical downloads may contain:

  • root-level DLL and PCK files
  • a named payload folder
  • a prebuilt mods/<Name>/ tree
  • an embedded legacy mod_manifest.json
  • a very small metadata-only PCK
  • a large PCK containing art, localization, scenes, and source artifacts

These shapes describe how an archive was published. They do not prove that it satisfies the current loader.

docs.title: Migration Rule For Legacy Archives
docs.text:
To test an older DLL/PCK pair on the current build:

  1. create mods/<ModId>/
  2. add a current <ModId>.json manifest
  3. rename payloads to <ModId>.dll and <ModId>.pck
  4. set has_dll and has_pck accurately
  5. rebuild against the current assemblies if the DLL does not load
  6. inspect old PCK paths before assuming localization or art remains compatible

An embedded legacy manifest can remain as inert pack content, but it is not a substitute for the external current manifest.

docs.title: General Lessons
docs.text:
• archive layout and installed layout are separate concerns
  • PCK size does not indicate whether a mod is valid
  • a code-heavy mod may still need a PCK for localization or icons
  • an asset-heavy mod may use little managed code
  • exact internal paths matter more than external archive names
  • old working releases are evidence for patterns, not current API authority

The files under examples/ are preserved as historical package inventories. Read their manifest observations as snapshots of older releases.

docs.title: Slay the Spire 2 Modding Handbook
docs.text: This handbook describes the current local modding contract of Slay the Spire 2 and then applies it to one coherent example containing a card, potion, relic, map event, and custom overlay. The game is the primary source: the installed assembly defines behavior, while the main PCK defines resource paths and localization conventions.

docs.title: Source Hierarchy
docs.text:
1. release_info.json, sts2.runtimeconfig.json, and the installed assemblies
  2. decompiled implementation in sts2.dll
  3. resources and localization in SlayTheSpire2.pck
  4. runtime logs and a clean installation test
  5. observed release packages and community documentation

This order matters during Early Access. A working pattern from an older release is evidence of what once worked, not proof of the current contract.

docs.text:
The tutorial was audited against the installed v0.107.1 assembly, its XML documentation, runtime configuration, and PCK. Loader behavior, hook ordering, model factories, UI stack methods, localization merging, and save-property serialization were traced in the decompiled implementation. Historical pack headers and contents were inspected separately.

Complete content and GUI class examples were compiled against the installed game DLLs. GUI source-generation output was also checked for callback bindings. Short fragments and placeholders are explanatory snippets rather than standalone projects.

The example mod has not been exercised in a running game during this audit.
